1.note: Here “Israel” is a metonym for the men of Israel. The word “all” is a generalization. Alternate translation: [the men of Israel were coming] (See also: [Hyperbole](ta:figs-hyperbole))

2.note: These are the names of men. See how you translated these names in 2 Chronicles 9:29.

3.note: Alternate translation: [the men of Israel sent for Jeroboam]
Alternate translation: [Jeroboam and all Israel came to Rehoboam]
Here “Israel” is a metonym for the men of Israel. The word “all” is a generalization. Alternate translation: [the men of Israel came] (See also: [Hyperbole](ta:figs-hyperbole))

4.note: A difficult yoke is a metaphor for very difficult labor and cruel treatment. Alternate translation: [treated us cruelly] or [forced us to work very hard]

4.q: make your father’s hard work easier, and lighten the heavy yoke that he put on us
4.note: These two phrases mean the same thing. The yoke metaphor emphasizes the fact that Solomon had treated them harshly. Alternate translation: [make the hard work that your father gave us easier, and do not treat us as harshly as he did] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

6.q: the old men who had stood before Solomon
6.note: To “stand before” is an idiom for serving the king in his presence. Alternate translation: [the old men who counseled Solomon] or [the old men who attended to Solomon]

6.q: to bring an answer to these people
6.note: Alternate translation: [to answer these people] or [to reply to these people]

8.note: Alternate translation: [Rehoboam did not follow the advice]

8.q: who had grown up with him, who stood before him
8.note: Alternate translation: [who were his long-time friends, and who advised him]

9.q: Lighten the yoke that your father put on us
9.note: To “lighten the yoke” is a metaphor that represents easing the burden. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 10:4. Alternate translation: [Do not treat us as cruelly as your father did] or [Do not force us to work as hard as your father did]

10.note: A heavy yoke is a metaphor for very difficult labor and cruel treatment. This metaphor is continued in this verses. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 10:4. Alternate translation: [treated them cruelly] or [forced them to work very hard]

10.q: My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist
10.note: This metaphor means that Rehoboam is more cruel and intimidating than his father. Alternate translation: [I rule much more harshly than my father ever did] or [I am much harsher than my father]

11.note: A heavy yoke is a metaphor for very difficult labor and cruel treatment. This metaphor is continued in this verses. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 10:4.

11.q: I will add to your yoke
11.note: “I will make your yoke heavier.” A yoke is a metaphor for labor. Alternate translation: [I will force you to work harder]

11.q: I will punish you with scorpions
11.note: Possible meanings are that: (1) “scorpions” is a metaphor for any kind of painful punishment. Alternate translation: [I will punish you much more harshly] or (2) [scorpions] is a metaphor for whips with sharp metal barbs at the end. Alternate translation: [I will punish you with whips that have sharp pieces of metal at the ends]

14.q: made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it
14.note: A heavy yoke is a metaphor for very difficult labor and cruel treatment. Alternate translation: [treated you cruelly, but I will be more cruel] or [forced you to work very hard, but I will make you work harder]

14.q: I will punish you with scorpions
14.note: Possible meanings are that: (1) “scorpions” is a metaphor for any kind of painful punishment. Alternate translation: [I will punish you much more harshly] or (2) [scorpions] is a metaphor for whips with sharp metal barbs at the end. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 10:11. Alternate translation: [I will punish you with whips that have sharp pieces of metal at the ends]

15.q: So the king did not listen to the people
15.note: Here “listen to the people” represents not care about what they said or about actually doing what they asked. Alternate translation: [So the king did not do what the people had asked him to do] or [So the king ignored the people]

15.q: it was a turn in events brought about by God
15.note: This is an idiom and can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [God caused things to happen like this] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

15.q: that Yahweh might carry out his word … Nebat
15.note: Alternate translation: [that Yahweh might do according to the message that he told Ahijah the Shilonite to tell Jeroboam son of Nebat] or [that Yahweh might do what he had said he would do when he told Ahijah the Shilonite to give a message to Jeroboam son of Nebat]

15.q: that Yahweh might carry out his word
15.note: The idiom “carry out his word” means to do what he had said he would do.

15.q: his word that Ahijah the Shilonite had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat
15.note: This refers to the message that God gave Ahijah to tell Jeroboam.

15.q: Ahijah the Shilonite … Jeroboam son of Nebat
15.note: See how you translated these names in 2 Chronicles 9:29.

16.note: Here “Israel” is a metonym for the men of Israel. The word “all” is a generalization. Alternate translation: [the men of Israel] (See also: [Hyperbole](ta:figs-hyperbole))

16.q: the king did not listen to them
16.note: Here “listen to the people” represents not caring about what they said or about actually doing what they asked. Alternate translation: [the king did not do what they had asked him to do] or [the king ignored them]

16.q: What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse
16.note: The people use this question and statement to imply that since they do not belong to David’s family, they are not obligated to support David’s grandson, King Rehoboam. Alternate translation: [We have no share in David. We will not have anything to do with the descendants of the son of Jesse] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

16.q: What share do we have in David?
16.note: Having a share in someone represents being his descendants and receiving the good things that descendants receive. Alternate translation: [We do not belong to the family of David]

16.q: We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse
16.note: “Son of Jesse” here is a metonym for David, a son of Jesse. Having an inheritance in someone represents being his descendants and receiving the good things that descendants receive. Alternate translation: [We will not receive any inheritance from the son of Jesse] or [We will have nothing to do with the his descendants]

16.q: Each of you should go back to his tent
16.note: “Tent” here is a metonym representing people’s homes. Alternate translation: [Go to your homes, people of Israel]

16.q: Now see to your own house, David
16.note: Here “see to” is an idiom meaning to take care of something, and “house” is a metonym for David’s lineage of power and prestige. Alternate translation: [Now take care of your own kingdom, descendant of David] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

18.note: Adoniram is the name of a man. In the Hebrew text of this sentence, his name was written as Adoram.

18.q: who was over the forced laborers
18.note: Being over people represents having authority to tell them what to do. Alternate translation: [who was in charge of the forced laborers]

18.q: stoned him to death with stones
18.note: Alternate translation: [killed Adoniram by stoning him]

19.note: Here “the house of David” represents the kings who were descendants of David. Alternate translation: [against the kings descended from David]
This refers to the general time when the author wrote this book. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 5:9. Alternate translation: [even now]
